Water company fined £250,000 for sewage pollution

13 February 2025

Dwr Cymru Welsh Water has been fined £250,000 for causing significant pollution to a river in Carmarthenshire.

The company appeared at Cardiff Crown Court on 13 February 2025 after pleading guilty to causing sewage to enter the River Towy in June 2023.

The court heard that a pump failure at the company's Llandeilo wastewater treatment works led to untreated sewage being discharged into the river for over 72 hours. The pollution affected a 5-kilometre stretch of the river, killing an estimated 3,000 fish including brown trout and salmon.

NRW officers responding to reports of dead fish traced the pollution back to the treatment works. An investigation found that the company had failed to maintain adequate backup systems and had delayed reporting the incident.

His Honour Judge David Hale said: "This was a serious incident that caused significant harm to an important Welsh river. The company's failure to maintain proper backup systems and their delay in reporting the incident aggravated the harm caused."

Dwr Cymru Welsh Water was fined £250,000 and ordered to pay £18,320 in prosecution costs.

The company has also agreed to fund a £150,000 river restoration project as part of the sentencing.

NRW's Director of Operations said: "We expect the highest standards from water companies when it comes to protecting our rivers. This fine reflects the seriousness of the pollution and sends a clear message that such failures will not be tolerated."

The offence was committed contrary to Regulation 12 of the Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016.
